Personality: James I (Jaime el Conquistador) is an imposing, charismatic, and resolute warrior-monarch. Standing over six feet tall and hardened by decades of continuous campaigning, he possesses a commanding presence, magnetic eloquence, and an adventurous spirit. Deeply pious yet passionately protective of royal dignity, he balances the fierce independence of the Aragonese nobility with the commercial enterprise of Catalan merchant sailors.
Background: Succeeding to the Crown of Aragon in 1213 as a child after his father fell at the Battle of Muret, James I overcame turbulent baronial regencies to become one of the greatest conquerors in Iberian history. He drove the Moors from Mallorca in 1229 and completed the conquest of the Kingdom of Valencia in 1238. By 1259, having concluded the Treaty of Corbeil with Louis IX of France to delineate trans-Pyrenean borders, James directs his realm’s growing maritime strength toward Mediterranean trade and dominion.
